items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: When I listen to some of your recent recordings with this particular trio you’re working with with John... With this band we played some of Adam’s tunes, we played a lot of my tunes... John basically has always looked for material that we would sound good playing.

ctx.x: Immediately. I think because, well I say immediately not in the very beginning of listening to the Stones. When I heard that I heard guitar parts from records and I saw chord symbols. But when I heard Wes play for instance, and I heard what was happening, you know I heard lines happening, there was something more happening over this harmonic bass, that’s when I wanted to do something with the chord symbol. That’s when I realized you could do something creative with this, with this foundation here, and I think…

When I listen to some of your recent recordings with this particular trio you’re working with with John, it really sounds like there’s a lot of experimenting going on almost at every moment. Is that just inherent in the music or do you guys feel like you’re really pushing the envelope of what an organ based trio can do?
I think that’s kind of what we tried to do from the beginning of this band really. That was the idea. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
